Rashi on Eruvin 72b:10:1.hebrew: ואיכא דאמרי כו' - ובהא פליגי: דב"ש סברי, אע"פ שרשות אחת היא ודמי לחמשה שעירבו ועירוב בא אצלן — אפילו הכי, כולהו בעי לערובי; וב"ה סברי: כיון דעירוב בא אצלן, לא:
Rashi on Eruvin 72b:10:1.english: And some say, etc. - And in this they disagree: For Beit Shammai hold [that] even though it is a single domain and is similar to five [people] who made an eiruv and an eiruv came to them, even so, all of them must make an eiruv; and Beit Hillel hold [that] since an eiruv came to them, [they do] not [need an eiruv for each group].

Rashi on Eruvin 72b:12:1.english: The partners - We do not read [this in the text].

Rashi on Eruvin 72b:12:2.english: And sleeping in their houses - And they, their father, and others reside in one courtyard.

Rashi on Eruvin 72b:12:3.hebrew: שצריכין עירוב לכל אחד ואחד - אם רוצין לערב עם שאר בני החצר, וטעמא מפרש בגמרא:
Rashi on Eruvin 72b:12:3.english: [That] an eiruv is required for each and every one - If they wish to make an eiruv with the rest of the residents of the courtyard; and the reason is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Eruvin 72b:12:4.english: He renounces his rights - He must renounce his rights.

Rashi on Eruvin 72b:13:1.hebrew: אימתי בזמן שמוליכין את עירובן - לתתו באחד מבתי שאר בני החצר. דהואיל והוזקקו לעירוב, אמרינן בגמרא: מגו דשאר דיורין אסרי, אינהו נמי אסרי, וצריכין כולן ליתן פת, הואיל וחלוקין דיוריהן בלינה ומקבלי פרס הן, כדמוקי בגמ' שאין אוכלין בבית אביהן ממש:
Rashi on Eruvin 72b:13:1.english: When? When they take their eiruv - To place it in one of the houses of the other residents of the courtyard. For since they were required to [join in] an eiruv, we say in the Gemara: Since the other residents forbid [carrying], they too forbid [it], and they all must contribute bread, since their residences are separate with respect to sleeping and they are recipients of an allowance, as [the Gemara] establishes in the Gemara that they do not actually eat in their father’s house.

Rashi on Eruvin 72b:13:2.hebrew: אבל אם היה - עירוב כל החצר בא לבית אביהן, שלא הוזקקו לעירוב, דאמרינן במי שהוציאוהו (לעיל עירובין דף מט.): ״בית שמניחין בו עירוב אין צריך ליתן את הפת״, והם כולם נמשכין בו:
Rashi on Eruvin 72b:13:2.english: But if [the eiruv] was - [That is, if] the eiruv of the entire courtyard comes to their father’s house, so that they are not obligated to [participate in] an eiruv, as we say in [the chapter] Mi Shehotzi’uhu (above, Eruvin 49a): “A house in which an eiruv is placed is not required to provide bread,” and they are all drawn after it [the father’s house].

Rashi on Eruvin 72b:13:3.english: Or if there are no other residents with them - For there are no residents who obligate him to [make] an eiruv.

Rashi on Eruvin 72b:13:4.english: They are not required to establish an eiruv - For they are like single individuals.

Rashi on Eruvin 72b:14:1.hebrew: שמעת מינה מקום לינה גורם - דאי הוו ישנים בבית אביהן, אפילו מוליכין עירובן למקום אחר, לא הוו צריכין לערובי אלא אביהם. ונימא: תיהוי תיובתיה דרב, דאמר לקמן בשמעתין "מקום פיתא גורם", והרי אלו אוכלין בבית אביהם, וחשבינן להו חלוקין:
Rashi on Eruvin 72b:14:1.english: Learn from it that the place of sleep determines - For if they were sleeping in their father’s house, even if they carry their eiruv to another place, only their father would need to contribute to the eiruv. And should we say: Let this be a refutation of Rav, who says later in our sugya, “The place of bread determines,” and yet these [brothers] eat in their father’s house, and we consider them divided?

Rashi on Eruvin 72b:14:2.hebrew: במקבלי פרס - הוצאה מבית אביהם, ואין אוכלין על שולחנו ממש:
Rashi on Eruvin 72b:14:2.english: With regard to those who receive a portion - [They receive an] allowance from their father's house, and they do not actually eat at his table.

Rashi on Eruvin 72b:1:1.english: The Keen - On account of his sharpness, they called him this.

Rashi on Eruvin 72b:2:1.hebrew: להך לישנא דאמר רב נחמן מחלוקת במסיפס - אבל במחיצות מודו ב"ה — תיובתא, דהא בהדיא קתני דבמחיצות שרו:
Rashi on Eruvin 72b:2:1.english: According to that version [in] which Rav Naḥman said: The dispute is regarding a mesifas - [implying that] but regarding partitions, Beit Hillel concede — [this is] a refutation, for behold, [the baraita] explicitly teaches that regarding partitions, they permit.

Rashi on Eruvin 72b:2:2.hebrew: אלא ללישנא בתרא - דקאמר דבמסיפס נמי אסרי ב"ש, מי לימא דתהוי הא תיובתיה, דקתני: במחיצות הוא דפליגי, הא במסיפס מודו:
Rashi on Eruvin 72b:2:2.english: Rather, according to the latter version - which said that Beit Shammai forbid even with a mesifas, shall we say that this is a refutation of his view, since it teaches: It is regarding partitions that they disagree, whereas with a mesifas they agree?

Rashi on Eruvin 72b:6:1.english: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda - That regarding partitions that reach the ceiling, they agree.

Rashi on Eruvin 72b:7:1.english: Actual rooms - That were never joined together.

Rashi on Eruvin 72b:8:1.hebrew: במה דברים אמורים - דאסרי ב"ש, כשהם מוליכין העירוב באחד משאר בתי החצר:
Rashi on Eruvin 72b:8:1.english: In what [case] is this said - That Beit Shammai forbid [relying on one eiruv is] when they bring the eiruv into one of the other houses of the courtyard.

Rashi on Eruvin 72b:8:2.hebrew: אבל אם היו - שאר בני החצר מביאין פיתן לטרקלין, דברי הכל כו'. והאי תנא, מדקא מפליג בין מקום אחר לבא אצלן, סבירא ליה טעמייהו דב"ש ובית הלל: לאו במחיצות פליגי, אלא אפי' לבית שמאי נמי טרקלין מחברן ואין צריך עירוב בינייהו, והוו להו כחמשה שגבו את עירובן. וסבירא להו דחמשה שעירבו את חצירן ובאין לערב עם חצר אחרת — אם מוליכין שם את עירובן, אין א' מהן שליח לכולן, אלא כולן צריכין ליתן פת; ואם עירוב בא בבית א' מהן, כולן שוין שם. והנך דטרקלין נמי, כיון דרשות אחת היא, להני דמו. דאי לבית שמאי רשויות חלוקות הן והן לא עירבו — כי עירוב בא אצלן, מאי הוי:
Rashi on Eruvin 72b:8:2.english: But if they were - [Meaning, if] the other residents of the courtyard were bringing their bread to the hall, “all agree, etc.” And this tanna, since he distinguishes between [taking the eiruv to] another place and [the eiruv] coming to them, holds that regarding the rationale of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel, they do not disagree about partitions; rather, even according to Beit Shammai, the hall unites them and no eiruv is needed among them, and they are [thus] considered like five [residents] who collected their eiruv. And they hold that [in the case of] five [residents] who made an eiruv for their courtyard and come to make an eiruv with another courtyard, if they carry their eiruv there, not [even] one of them [can serve as] an agent for all of them, but rather all of them must contribute bread; but if the eiruv comes to the house of one of them, they are all equal there. And these [residents] of the hall as well, since it is a single domain, are comparable to them. For if according to Beit Shammai they are separate domains and they did not make an eiruv [among themselves], when the eiruv comes to them, what does it accomplish?

Rashi on Eruvin 72b:9:1.english: Who collected their eiruv - Who reside in a courtyard and made an eiruv for their courtyard.

Tosafot on Eruvin 72b:14:1.hebrew: במקבלי פרס שנו - ואע"פ דמקום פיתא ולינה בבתיהם, אהני מה שאוכלים משל אביהם — דאם היה עירוב בא אצלם או שאין עמהם דיורין, אין צריכין לערב:
Tosafot on Eruvin 72b:14:1.english: They taught [this] with regard to those who receive a portion - And even though the place of bread and [the place of] sleeping are in their [own] houses, the fact that they eat from their father['s provisions] is effective, in that if the eiruv was coming to them, or if there are no [other] residents with them, they do not need to make an eiruv.

Tosafot on Eruvin 72b:15:1.hebrew: מי שיש לו בית שער אינו אוסר עליו - אע"פ שדרין בו, כדתנן לקמן בפרק כיצד משתתפין (עירובין דף פה:). ואם תאמר: אי בבית שער דבית, תיפוק ליה משום בית, דאסר על בני החצר אע"פ שאין דרין בו, מידי דהוה אבית התבן? וי"ל: כגון שנתן בעל הבית עירובו, וקמ"ל דהדר בבית שער לא בעי לערב, דלא אסר:
Tosafot on Eruvin 72b:15:1.english: "One who has a gatehouse does not render it prohibited for him" - Even though people reside in it, as we learned below in the chapter [entitled] Keitzad Mishtatefin (Eruvin 85b). And if you say: If [this is referring to] a gatehouse of a house, let [the prohibition] be derived on account of the house, which prohibits the residents of the courtyard even though no one resides in it, just as is the case with a straw storehouse! And one can say: For example, where the homeowner contributed his eiruv, and [the baraita] teaches us that one who resides in the gatehouse does not need to join the eiruv, as he does not render it prohibited.

Tosafot on Eruvin 72b:1:1.hebrew: רבי יהודה הסבר - רבינו חננאל גריס: "הסבך". פירוש: גדיל לסבכה, כעין מצנפת וכובע, כמו "שבכים מעשה שבכה" (מלכים א ז׳:י״ז). א"נ, על שם עירו, דבספר יהושע (טו), כמו כן כתיב: "מדין וסבכה":
Tosafot on Eruvin 72b:1:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda the Keen [hasabbar] - Rabbeinu Chananel reads [the name as] HaSavakh. Explanation: A braid for a hairnet, a kind of turban and cap, like "nets of checker-work" (I Kings 7:17). Alternatively, [he was named] after his town, as in the Book of Joshua (chapter 15), it is likewise written: "Middin and Sevakhah."

Tosafot on Eruvin 72b:5:1.hebrew: כח דהיתרא עדיף ליה - לא שייך הכא למיפרך: "ליפלגו בתרוייהו", כדפריך בריש ביצה (דף ב:) — דהתם, כדי להודיע כחן דבית הלל דאוסרין, הוה ליה לאשמעי' בתרוייהו, משום דכח דהיתרא עדיף — דב"ש לא חשיבי ליה כ"כ, דב"ש במקום ב"ה אינה משנה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 72b:5:1.english: The strength of a permissive ruling is preferable to him - It is not applicable here to challenge: "Let them disagree in both of them," as [the Gemara] challenges at the beginning of Beitzah (2b) — for there, in order to inform [us] of the strength of Beit Hillel who prohibit, it should have let us hear [the dispute] in both of them, because the strength of permission is preferable — [for here,] Beit Shammai are not so important to him, as [the opinion of] Beit Shammai in place of Beit Hillel is not a Mishnah.

Tosafot on Eruvin 72b:6:1.hebrew: אמר ר"נ אמר רב הלכה כרבי יהודה - אע"ג דאותבי' מינה לל"ק דר"נ, אתיא כלישנא בתרא:
Tosafot on Eruvin 72b:6:1.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rav said: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda - Even though we raised an objection from it against the first version of Rav Naḥman, [this statement] follows the latter version.

Tosafot on Eruvin 72b:8:1.hebrew: אבל אם היה עירוב בא אצלן דברי הכל עירוב אחד לכולן - וא"ת: טעמא דב"ש אתא לאשמעינן?! דלב"ה לא איצטריך, דאפילו מוליכין עירובן אמר עירוב אחד לכולן! וכי האי גוונא פריך במס' שבת בפ' ר"א דמילה (שבת ד' קלה.). וי"ל: דלב"ה נמי נפקא מינה — דכעין חדרים ועליות, דדווקא במוליכין עירובן קאמר דמודו שצריכין עירוב לכל חבורה וחבורה, אבל בעירוב בא אצלן עירוב אחד לכולן; דכעין חדרים ועליות לב"ה כמו מחיצות שאין מגיעות לתקרה לב"ש. ומיהו, בחדרים ועליות ממש אין נראה לחלק בין מוליכין עירובן לעירוב בא אצלן, מדפשיט ליה כ"כ להש"ס דקאמר: "אילימא חדרים ועליות ממש — פשיטא":
Tosafot on Eruvin 72b:8:1.english: "But if their eiruv was coming to them, all agree that one eiruv [suffices] for all of them" - And if you say: Did [the Tanna] come to teach us the reasoning of Beit Shammai?! For according to Beit Hillel, it was not necessary [to state this], as even when they bring their eiruv [elsewhere, Beit Hillel] said [that] one eiruv [suffices] for all of them! And in a similar vein, [the Gemara] challenges in Tractate Shabbat, in the chapter [entitled] "Rabbi Eliezer Demilah" (Shabbat 135a). And one can say: According to Beit Hillel as well there is a practical difference — regarding [partitions that are] like rooms and upper stories; for it was specifically when they bring their eiruv [elsewhere] that [the Mishnah] stated that they concede that they require an eiruv for each and every group, but when the eiruv comes to them, one eiruv [suffices] for all of them; for [partitions that are] like rooms and upper stories according to Beit Hillel are like partitions that do not reach the ceiling according to Beit Shammai. However, in [the case of] actual rooms and upper stories, it does not appear [correct] to distinguish between bringing their eiruv [elsewhere] and the eiruv coming to them, since it was so obvious to the Gemara, which said: "If we say actual rooms and actual upper stories, it is obvious!"

Tosafot on Eruvin 72b:9:1.hebrew: כמאן כבית הלל - וליכא למימר דאתיא כב"ש, וברייתא באין עמהם דיורין, כדאוקמינן לה לקמן, אבל במתניתין כשיש עמהן דיורין, דמיגו דהני אסרי אהדדי הני נמי אסרי; דהיכי דמי הני דיורין? אי בחצר קיימי — מ"מ כל הטרקלין חשיב כחדא, ומטלטלין זה עם זה בכל הטרקלין בלא עירוב כשיש דיורין בחצר כמו שאין דיורין בחצר. ואי בעו ביניהם עירוב כשיש עמהן דיורין בחצר, הכי נמי ליבעי כשאין עמהן דיורין, דמה ענין דיורין בחצר לגבי הטרקלין? ומיהו ה"מ למימר: כגון שיש בטרקלין דמתניתין חדרים ועליות גמורין שאין להם פתח בחצר אלא יוצאין דרך טרקלין, דמיגו דהני אסרי, הנך ה' חבורות נמי אסרי; אבל לא משמע ליה לאוקמי מתניתין בהכי. ועוד, דדילמא בהא הוו מודו ב"ה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 72b:9:1.english: "In accordance with whose opinion? In accordance with Beit Hillel" - And it cannot be said that [the baraita] follows Beit Shammai, and the baraita [deals with a case] where there are no [other] residents with them, as we establish later (73a), whereas our Mishnah is [a case] where there are [other] residents with them, so that since these [other residents] restrict one another, these [groups in the hall] also restrict [one another]; for what is the case of these residents? If they reside in the courtyard — nevertheless, the entire hall is considered like one [domain], and [the groups] carry with one another throughout the hall without an eiruv when there are residents in the courtyard just as when there are no residents in the courtyard. And if they require an eiruv among themselves when there are residents with them in the courtyard, so too they should require [an eiruv] when there are no residents with them, for what bearing do residents in the courtyard have upon the hall? However, [the Gemara] could have said: for example, where there are in the hall of our Mishnah complete rooms and upper stories that have no doorway into the courtyard, but rather they exit through the hall, so that since these [residents of the rooms] restrict, those five groups also restrict; but it did not seem reasonable to [the Gemara] to establish our Mishnah in such [a case]. And furthermore, perhaps in that case Beit Hillel would also concede [that each group requires an eiruv].
